scope: Original AQA AS 7356 B9 / A-level 7357 3.3 Year 1 Pure first school mock: six manually reviewed graph transformation sketches (36 marks)
notes: All plotted graphs require an actual sketch/photo and manual mark-point review: textual keywords are not a substitute. These are original problems, not AQA copyrighted questions or official mark schemes. Excludes A2-only modulus transformations, stats, mechanics and radians.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original AQA AS Pure Function Transformation Sketches
questions.question: Translate a quadratic and sketch its features
questions.prompt: The original curve is y=f(x)=x²−4, passing through (−2,0), (0,−4), (2,0). Sketch y=g(x)=f(x−3)+2 on axes. Label its turning point, the two transformed points from (−2,0) and (2,0), its x-intercepts and its y-intercept. [6 marks]
markPoints: Correctly applies a translation 3 units right and 2 units up to every point of the original graph.
Draws an upward-opening parabola with turning point (3,−2) and symmetry axis x=3.
Maps the two given original x-axis points to (1,2) and (5,2).
Labels the exact x-intercepts as (3−√2,0) and (3+√2,0).
Finds and labels the y-intercept (0,7).
Sketch is consistent with g(x)=(x−3)²−2 and includes axes and correctly placed key features.
questions.modelAnswer: g(x)=(x−3)²−2. Every original point (u,v) maps to (u+3,v+2). Thus (−2,0)→(1,2), (0,−4)→(3,−2), (2,0)→(5,2). It opens upwards, axis x=3, crosses x-axis at x=3±√2 and y-axis at (0,7).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original AQA AS Pure Function Transformation Sketches
questions.question: Reflect and rescale a parabola with horizontal input
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=x² and g(x)=−2f(2x+4)+1. Draw a sketch of y=g(x), showing its turning point, its line of symmetry, the images of the original points (−1,1) and (1,1), and both exact x-intercepts. Show how the input and output transformations act on coordinates. [6 marks]
markPoints: Correctly rewrites g(x)=−8(x+2)²+1.
Maps an original point (u,v) to (u/2−2,−2v+1).
Places the two transformed points at (−5/2,−1) and (−3/2,−1).
Marks the maximum turning point (−2,1) and vertical symmetry axis x=−2.
Gives the exact x-intercepts as x=−2±√2/4.
Sketch is a downward-opening parabola consistent with the points, vertex and intercepts.
questions.modelAnswer: g(x)=−2(2x+4)²+1=−8(x+2)²+1. Map (u,v)→(u/2−2,−2v+1). Original (−1,1)→(−5/2,−1); (1,1)→(−3/2,−1); the vertex (0,0)→(−2,1). Solve −8(x+2)²+1=0 to get x=−2±√2/4. Sketch a downward parabola with axis x=−2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original AQA AS Pure Function Transformation Sketches
questions.question: Translate a reciprocal curve and its asymptotes
questions.prompt: The curve is y=f(x)=1/x. Sketch y=g(x)=f(x−2)+3. Clearly show and label both asymptotes, the transformed points corresponding to (1,1) and (−1,−1), the x-intercept and the y-intercept. [6 marks]
markPoints: Applies a translation right by 2 and up by 3 to obtain g(x)=1/(x−2)+3.
Draws and labels vertical asymptote x=2.
Draws and labels horizontal asymptote y=3.
Finds x-intercept (5/3,0) and y-intercept (0,5/2).
Sketch places one branch above y=3 for x>2 and the other below y=3 for x<2 without crossing the asymptotes.
questions.modelAnswer: Translation by (+2,+3) gives g(x)=1/(x−2)+3. Asymptotes x=2 and y=3. Original points map (1,1)→(3,4) and (−1,−1)→(1,2). For y=0, x=5/3; for x=0, y=5/2. Right branch lies above y=3; left branch lies below y=3.

questions.series: Original AQA AS Pure Function Transformation Sketches
questions.question: Reflect a quadratic horizontally then translate vertically
questions.prompt: The function f(x)=x²−2x−3 has a minimum at (1,−4). Sketch y=h(x)=f(−x)+2. Show the transformation of coordinates, turning point, x-intercepts and y-intercept; explain which axis is the reflection axis. [5 marks]
markPoints: Identifies reflection in the y-axis followed by translation 2 units upwards.
Maps original (u,v) to (−u,v+2), locating the new minimum at (−1,−2).
Derives h(x)=(x+1)²−2.
Calculates exact x-intercepts x=−1±√2.
Labels the y-intercept (0,−1) and sketches an upwards-opening parabola with axis x=−1.
questions.modelAnswer: f(x)=(x−1)²−4. Replacing x by −x reflects in the y-axis, mapping (u,v)→(−u,v). Adding 2 shifts up, so overall (u,v)→(−u,v+2). h(x)=x²+2x−1=(x+1)²−2, vertex (−1,−2), roots −1±√2, y-intercept −1.

questions.series: Original AQA AS Pure Function Transformation Sketches
questions.question: Draw cubic reflection and horizontal compression
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=x³−3x and g(x)=f(−2x). Sketch y=g(x), labelling all three x-intercepts and both stationary points. Explain where the original points (−1,2) and (1,−2) move, and state the effect on the graph's horizontal scale and orientation. [7 marks]
markPoints: Describes reflection in the y-axis and horizontal scale factor 1/2 (order may vary for this combination).
Maps an original point (u,v) to (−u/2,v).
Expands g(x)=−8x³+6x.
Finds all three x-intercepts x=−√3/2, 0 and +√3/2.
Finds stationary x-coordinates from g′(x)=−24x²+6=0, giving x=−1/2 and 1/2.
Labels stationary points (−1/2,−2) local minimum and (1/2,2) local maximum, consistent with transformed original points.
Sketch has correct decreasing cubic end behaviour as x increases, crossing the origin and the other two zeros.
questions.modelAnswer: Replacing x with −2x reflects in the y-axis and compresses horizontally by factor 1/2. Each (u,v)→(−u/2,v). Hence (−1,2)→(1/2,2) and (1,−2)→(−1/2,−2). g(x)=−8x³+6x=−2x(4x²−3). Roots −√3/2,0,+√3/2. g′=−24x²+6, so extrema at (−1/2,−2) and (1/2,2). Left end rises, right end falls.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original AQA AS Pure Function Transformation Sketches
questions.question: Sketch a translated and stretched inverse-square curve
questions.prompt: Start with f(x)=1/x². Sketch y=g(x)=3f(x+1)−2. Label both asymptotes, the transformed points corresponding to (−1,1) and (1,1), the y-intercept and the two exact x-intercepts. Show both branches clearly. [6 marks]
markPoints: Recognises translation 1 unit left, vertical scale factor 3 and translation 2 units down, giving g(x)=3/(x+1)²−2.
Labels the vertical asymptote x=−1.
Labels the horizontal asymptote y=−2.
Finds both x-intercepts x=−1±√(3/2) and the y-intercept (0,1).
Sketch shows two branches above y=−2 on either side of x=−1, rising towards +∞ near the vertical asymptote.
questions.modelAnswer: g(x)=3/(x+1)²−2. For f(ax+b) here a=1 and b=1, all x coordinates move 1 left; outputs triple and decrease by 2. Thus (−1,1)→(−2,1), (1,1)→(0,1). Asymptotes x=−1, y=−2. Solve 3/(x+1)²−2=0: (x+1)²=3/2, so x=−1±√(3/2). At x=0, y=1. Both branches are above the horizontal asymptote.
